preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership)
Contract must have ETH balance (from accumulated fees or direct transfers)

violation_target.exploit_hint: Become the contract owner (or compromise the current owner), then call setOperationsAddress() to set the operations address to a malicious contract you control. The swapBack() function will send all contract ETH to operationsAddress via a low-level call. Create a malicious contract that receives ETH and transfers it to the attacker. Alternatively, if already owner, directly call withdrawStuckETH() which also uses an uncontrolled low-level call to drain ETH to msg.sender.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The FoundationToken contract has two uncontrolled low-level calls that allow draining ETH: 1) swapBack() sends all contract ETH to operationsAddress, 2) withdrawStuckETH() sends all contract ETH to msg.sender (owner). Both are protected by onlyOwner modifier. The vulnerability is that if an attacker gains ownership, they can drain all ETH from the contract.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Gain ownership of the contract by spoofing the current owner. 2. Send ETH to the contract to give it a balance. 3. Call withdrawStuckETH() to drain all ETH to ourselves.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the current owner. 2. Call transferOwnership() to make ourselves the owner. 3. Send ETH to the contract using deal() or direct transfer. 4. Call withdrawStuckETH() as the new owner to drain ETH. 5. Verify our ETH balance increased.
